neighbours.label: proper names from Tolkien's Middle-earth (Mordor, Gondor, Gorbag), as against historical or other fictional place and person names in the same war-story sentences
fire: After the battle, the riders returned to the white city of Gondor.
Sauron's eye watched over the plains of Mordor day and night.
The orc Gorbag argued with his captain about the prisoner.
The road to Mordor led through marshes and dead hills.
Many soldiers of Gondor fell defending the river crossing.
Beyond the mountains lay Mordor, black and silent under ash.
The steward of Gondor refused to give up his chair.
Scouts from Mordor were seen near the eastern pass.
quiet: After the battle, the riders returned to the white city of Toledo.
The emperor's spies watched over the plains of Persia day and night.
The pirate Blackbeard argued with his captain about the prisoner.
The road to Moscow led through marshes and frozen hills.
Many soldiers of Sparta fell defending the narrow pass.
Beyond the mountains lay Tibet, cold and silent under snow.
The steward of the castle refused to give up his chair.
Scouts from Prussia were seen near the eastern pass.
